$description: Kiso design tokens — DTCG 2025.10. color.* is the primitive palette, semantic.* is the published colour roles (emitted as --color-<role>), accent.* restates the roles that follow the accent hue per accent (emitted as one [data-accent] block each), and the remaining groups are the non-colour scales: font, type, spacing, radius, size, corner, hatch, shadow, motion, breakpoint. A role whose two themes differ carries both in $extensions.mode and is emitted as one CSS light-dark() declaration resolved by color-scheme; the dark value is also the plain $value. Components consume semantic.* and the scale tokens only.

color.$description: Primitive layer — the raw palette. Not consumed directly by components.

white.$description: Pure white. Light theme elevated surface.

black.$description: Pure black. Reserved for overlays and shadows.

50.$description: Lightest neutral. Light-theme elevated surface above neutral.100.

950.$description: Darkest neutral. Retained for compatibility; the dark theme's sidebar is dark.950.

neutral.$description: Warm neutral ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). The light theme consumes 50-600; the dark theme moved to the dedicated dark ramp, so this ramp's darker steps are retained but no longer referenced. Warm grey rather than the marketing site's cool slate: the surfaces carry the calm, which lets the accent stay saturated without shouting.

100.$description: Foreground on dark. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on every dark surface.

450.$description: Half step. Strong lines and subtle text share it on dark (border-strong, subtle-foreground), as neutral.500 does for both roles on light: dark.500 misses the 3:1 non-text gate on dark.800 and dark.700.

500.$description: Free step between the 450 split and the border pair. Not referenced by the semantic layer: 2.6:1 on dark.800 fails the 3:1 non-text gate.

700.$description: Elevated surfaces, muted and secondary fills on dark.

950.$description: Darkest step. Sidebar on dark, and danger-foreground on a danger fill.

dark.$description: Dedicated dark-theme neutral ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest), in the light ramp's warm hue so both themes read as one product. It replaces the cold, purple-leaning dark steps the dark theme used to borrow from neutral, and its layer spacing gives every surface a clear step off its neighbour: the sidebar sinks below the canvas, the card lifts above it.

50.$description: Lightest lilac. Light-theme tinted surface (row hover, ghost hover).

500.$description: Mid lilac. Closes the ramp between 400 and 600; accent.base stays the mode-aware base.

950.$description: Darkest lilac. Retained ramp step; the dark accent tints are dedicated literals on the semantic layer.

violet.$description: Violet accent ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). The default accent. Lilac accent, 50 to 950. The ramp's 500 is a plain step; the base accent is its own primitive (accent.base), mode-aware because each theme takes the value where it measures strongest. This is the two-layer resolution of the missing-500 wrinkle.

base.$description: Base accent primitive and the theme ink: deeper violet on light (6.36:1 on background), light lilac on dark (6.36:1 on background, 5.5:1 on surface). Flows into link and focus; the deep fill role lives on semantic.primary.
The terracotta ink: text-eligible in both themes.

terracotta.$description: Terracotta accent ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). Same lightness per step as the violet ramp, hue rotated to 48 in OKLCH, so every role keeps its contrast.

base.$description: The teal ink: text-eligible in both themes.

teal.$description: Teal accent ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). Same lightness per step as the violet ramp, hue rotated to 185 in OKLCH, so every role keeps its contrast.

base.$description: The cobalt ink: text-eligible in both themes.

cobalt.$description: Cobalt accent ramp, 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). Same lightness per step as the violet ramp, hue rotated to 258 in OKLCH, so every role keeps its contrast.

50.$description: Lightest lilac. Light-theme tinted surface (row hover, ghost hover).

500.$description: Mid lilac. Closes the ramp between 400 and 600; accent.base stays the mode-aware base.

950.$description: Darkest lilac. Retained ramp step; the dark accent tints are dedicated literals on the semantic layer.

accent.$description: The active accent ramp. Aliases the violet ramp by default; each accent.<name> group remaps it to another ramp, so semantic roles that reference color.accent.* follow the chosen accent without restating.

base.$description: Base accent primitive and the theme ink: deeper violet on light (6.36:1 on background), light lilac on dark (6.36:1 on background, 5.5:1 on surface). Flows into link and focus; the deep fill role lives on semantic.primary.

status.$description: Status primitives, mode-aware: each theme needs a different lightness to hold AA as text. Kept fully saturated on purpose — with a calm surface set, state is what earns colour.

danger.$description: Danger status primitive. The dark step sits at 4.6:1 on elevated-surface; a darker red missed AA there.

semantic.$description: Semantic layer — the published colour roles. Each aliases a primitive or another role; a role whose two themes differ carries both in $extensions.mode and is emitted as a single light-dark() declaration. Emitted as --color-<role>.

background.$description: App canvas. Surface role, never text.

surface.$description: Cards, panels, table rows. Surface role.

foreground.$description: Primary text. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

muted-foreground.$description: Secondary text, labels. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

subtle-foreground.$description: Placeholders, timestamps, hints. Large text and non-essential metadata only (>=3:1). Never body copy. On dark this is dark.450, because dark.500 misses 3:1 on the dark surfaces.

border.$description: Dividers and input outlines. Non-text role.

primary.$description: Primary fill: primary buttons, solid badges, checked controls, the brand mark. Deep violet in both themes; on dark it is a dedicated fill and is not text-eligible, so ink roles (link, focus) take accent.base instead.

accent.$description: Emphasis and highlight. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

success.$description: Positive state. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

warning.$description: Caution state. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

danger.$description: Destructive or error state. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

info.$description: Neutral informational state. Text-eligible: passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes.

focus.$description: Focus ring. Non-text role. >=3:1 against background. The light ink: alias of accent.base in both themes.

disabled.$description: Disabled text and controls. Exempt from contrast minimums per WCAG 1.4.3.

card.$description: Panel and card fill. Alias of surface, named for the component that owns it.

popover.$description: Menus, dialogs, command palette. Alias of elevated-surface.

muted.$description: Recessed fill one step off card: table headers, card footers, segmented tracks. Surface role.

sidebar.$description: Application shell navigation column. Sits below the canvas on dark, above it on light.

border-strong.$description: Emphasised line: hover outlines, switch tracks, chart gridlines, corner marks. Non-text role, >=3:1 on background, surface and elevated-surface in both themes. On dark this is dark.450, sharing the subtle-text step as neutral.500 does on light.

primary-foreground.$description: Text and icons on a primary fill. Near-white on the deep violet fill in both themes. Passes AA on primary in both themes.

primary-hover.$description: Primary fill on hover - one step brighter than primary, keeping primary-foreground legible.

link.$description: Inline and standalone links. The light ink: alias of accent.base in both themes, so links stay text-eligible where the primary fill is not.

accent-surface.$description: Faintest accent tint: row hover, ghost-button hover. Non-text role.

accent-surface-hover.$description: Accent tint one step stronger. Non-text role.

selected.$description: Selected row, active navigation item, highlighted palette result. One ramp step past accent-surface-hover, so a selected item and a hovered sibling never paint the same surface. Non-text role.

secondary.$description: Neutral button fill, range track, count badge. Non-text role.

secondary-hover.$description: Secondary fill on hover. Non-text role.

ring.$description: Focus ring, drag handle active state. Alias of focus, named for the property it sets.

disabled-surface.$description: Fill of a disabled control. Exempt from contrast minimums per WCAG 1.4.3.

overlay.$description: Scrim behind a modal layer. Non-text role.

hatch.$description: Hatch stripe marking a region that is not data. One step off the surface it sits on — never raise it further, it is a texture, not a message.

shadow-hairline.$description: Shadow colour for the 1px contact shadow under a resting control.

shadow-contact.$description: Shadow colour for separated and floating layers. Darker on dark, where a shadow has to work harder.

success-surface.$description: Success tinted fill for badges and callouts — the success hue at low alpha. Non-text role.

success-border.$description: Success outline for badges and callouts. Non-text role.

warning-surface.$description: Warning tinted fill for badges and callouts — the warning hue at low alpha. Non-text role.

warning-border.$description: Warning outline for badges and callouts. Non-text role.

danger-surface.$description: Danger tinted fill for badges and callouts — the danger hue at low alpha. Non-text role.

danger-border.$description: Danger outline for badges and callouts. Non-text role.

info-surface.$description: Info tinted fill for badges and callouts — the info hue at low alpha. Non-text role.

info-border.$description: Info outline for badges and callouts. Non-text role.

danger-foreground.$description: Text and icons on a danger fill. Inverts with the fill, like primary-foreground: white on the light-theme red, near-black on the dark-theme salmon.

warning-on-dark.$description: Warning on a permanently dark surface (log view, terminal). Theme-invariant on purpose: the surface does not follow color-scheme, so neither can the text.

danger-on-dark.$description: Danger on a permanently dark surface (log view, terminal). Theme-invariant on purpose: the surface does not follow color-scheme, so neither can the text.

info-on-dark.$description: Info on a permanently dark surface (log view, terminal). Theme-invariant on purpose: the surface does not follow color-scheme, so neither can the text.

chart-1.$description: Categorical chart series 1. Identity only, never status. Pair with its numbered label, interactive highlighting, and exact values. Pinned to the violet ink: chart series do not follow the accent, so the palette stays distinguishable from the status series under every accent.

chart-2.$description: Categorical chart series 2. Identity only, never status. Pair with its numbered label, interactive highlighting, and exact values.

chart-3.$description: Categorical chart series 3. Identity only, never status. Pair with its numbered label, interactive highlighting, and exact values.

chart-4.$description: Categorical chart series 4. Identity only, never status. Pair with its numbered label, interactive highlighting, and exact values.

chart-5.$description: Categorical chart series 5. Identity only, never status. Pair with its numbered label, interactive highlighting, and exact values.

accent.$description: Accent themes. Each child restates the roles that follow the accent hue and is emitted as one [data-accent="<name>"] block; the ramp entries remap --color-accent-* to the named primitive ramp so every alias of the ramp follows without restating it. violet equals the :root default. The hue accents leave the neutral roles alone: the warm grey carries the interface and only the accent changes. nocturne is a full neutral palette and restates them.

primary.$description: The primary fill. Light: the ink. Dark: a deeper fill that is not text-eligible.
The primary fill. Light: the ink. Dark: a deeper fill that is not text-eligible.
The primary fill. Light: the ink. Dark: a deeper fill that is not text-eligible.
The primary fill. Light: the ink. Dark: a deeper fill that is not text-eligible.

base.$description: The nocturne ink: the site's link colour, text-eligible in both themes.

nocturne.$description: The marketing site's palette: cool slate neutrals (hue 278) under the violet ink, so the ramp is violet and the neutral roles are restated. Text and border roles follow the slate; the accent roles keep the site's own values.

font.$description: Font families. Inter for heading and body - hierarchy comes from size and weight, not a second family. JetBrains Mono for code and data. Keeps the marketing site stack, with system fallbacks added.

heading.$description: Heading family. Inter, same as body; headings differentiate by size and weight.

body.$description: Body family. Inter for interface text.

mono.$description: Monospace family. Code and machine-readable values (hashes, identifiers). Numeric tables use body with tabular figures, not mono.

type.$description: Type scale for dense product UI: 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 22, 30. Tighter than a modular ramp on purpose — the steps a console actually uses, each distinguishable from its neighbour at 14px body. role.* assembles the steps into the published text roles: display, heading, body, label, metadata, code, numeric.

label.$description: Labels, buttons, form captions, small UI text.

body.$description: Body copy and control text; base size for code and numeric text. 14px, not 16px: a console is read at desk distance, in density.

display.$description: Display headings and stat values — the calm ceiling.

relaxed.$description: Long-form reading, notes. 1.6 is rationalized - 1.75 is part of the ad-hoc set and is deliberately not reused.

snug.$description: Section and card headings — between tight and normal.

heading.$description: Display and headings - a hair tighter than body.

normal.$description: Neutral tracking - the default for body, metadata and code roles.

display.$description: Display headings and stat values — tighter still than heading.

caps.$description: Uppercase eyebrow labels, which need tracking opened up to stay readable.

heading.$description: Page headings (h1); h2 and h3 step down through type.size.

numeric.$description: Numeric and tabular data. Carries the namespaced com.momoi-labs.kiso.fontVariantNumeric extension (tabular-nums), emitted by the formatter as the global --font-variant-numeric feature token.

spacing.$description: Spacing scale on a 4px base, with a 2px hairline step below it: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64.

2xs.$description: Hairline gaps: segmented-control padding, stacked label/value pairs.

radius.$description: Corner radii. Near-square on purpose: a blueprint frame is drawn, not rounded. Panels use radius.surface (0) and get their corner treatment from corner.* instead; the small radii only take the bite off controls.

xs.$description: Checkboxes, chart bars, the smallest controls.

md.$description: Buttons, inputs, menu items. The control default.

lg.$description: Segmented-control tracks and other control groups.

surface.$description: Panels, cards, tables, dialogs. Square, always — corner marks read as registration marks only against a square frame.

shadow.$description: Elevation scale. The colour is a token (color.shadow.*) rather than a literal, so a shadow deepens with the theme instead of staying a fixed black at a fixed alpha; the geometry here is deliberately shallow.

xs.$description: Resting controls: buttons, inputs, selected segments. A contact line, not a shadow.

sm.$description: Cards and panels on the canvas — subtle separation.

lg.$description: Dialogs, drawers and the command palette — the only layers that float free.

motion.$description: Motion - minimal (calm): two durations for the few allowed transitions (focus/hover, open/close) and one standard ease-out easing. The generated CSS includes a prefers-reduced-motion gate that zeroes every duration.

standard.$description: Ease-out - elements settle, no bounce, no delight for its own sake.

breakpoint.$description: Responsive breakpoints (min-width). Desktop and mobile principles: mobile-first, then small tablets, desktop, wide desktop.

size.$description: Control and layout sizes. control.* is the height of a single-line control; it is the token the 44px touch target is NOT. Kiso separates the two on purpose: 44px is a WCAG target for coarse pointers, and applying it on the desktop is what makes a dense console look like a toy.

control.$description: Height of a single-line control: button, input, select, menu item.

lg.$description: Primary calls to action, table row height.

touch.$description: Accessibility minimum, not a control size.

min.$description: WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum. Apply only inside @media (pointer: coarse) — as a min-height on top of a control size, never as the control size itself.

icon.$description: Icon box sizes. Icons are stroked, not filled, and inherit currentColor.

sm.$description: Icons inside labels, badges and xs controls.

md.$description: The default. Icons in buttons, inputs, navigation.

max.$description: Maximum content measure. Beyond this a row is scanned, not read.

corner.$description: Corner registration marks — the blueprint corner treatment, and the replacement for a rounded corner. Two 1px ticks per corner, each lying along the frame line it extends and stopping corner.mark-gap short of it, so the mark points at the corner without touching it. Two ticks, not four: the other two arms of a cross land on top of the panel border and are invisible.

mark.$description: Marks on (1) or off (0). Opacity, so it is a single switch on the pseudo-element rather than a rule per component.

mark-gap.$description: Distance from tick end to the frame it points at. The gap is the mark — close it and this is just a thicker border.

hatch.$description: Diagonal hatch marking a region that is not data: an empty state, a chrome band, an unavailable pane. Companion to the corner marks.

period.$description: Stripe-to-stripe distance. Half of it is stripe, half is gap.

angle.$description: Stripe angle. DTCG has no angle type, so the CSS unit rides in the namespaced extension and the formatter emits "45deg".
